finding.claim: The /checkout endpoint computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set arbitrary prices, including zero or negative values, or negative quantities, to pay less than the real price or get a negative charge (a refund). The /checkout-v2 handler looks prices up server-side, which shows the intended design.
finding.source: req.body.items[].price and req.body.items[].qty in the POST /checkout request body, supplied by any authenticated user

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, both taken directly from the request body
the unvalidated total is passed to payments.charge
the total is returned to the client as the charged amount

finding.guards_checked: No server-side catalog price lookup, no numeric validation, no check for negative values or non-numbers, and no minimum on qty. Only one file exists in the repo, so no middleware or validation can be seen. The mounting of this router and any auth middleware that sets req.user are not visible. Even if authentication exists, the price is still client-controlled.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no validation and cart.js:6 passes it to payments.charge, while /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) does a server-side price lookup and clamps qty, showing the intended control is missing here.

finding.claim: The /checkout-v2 endpoint does not validate i.qty or the catalog price. Math.floor(NaN) is NaN, and Math.max(1, NaN) is NaN, so a non-numeric qty such as a string or undefined makes total NaN. Infinity passes through as Infinity. Fractional quantities are floored, which is fine. An unknown sku may make price return undefined, which also gives NaN. The result is a NaN or Infinity charge amount passed to the payment provider, with unpredictable behavior. Very large qty values can also cause overflow or abnormally large charges. This is a weaker, input-validation issue.
finding.source: req.body.items[].qty and req.body.items[].sku in the POST /checkout-v2 request body

trace.note: iterates over the client-supplied items array without checking that it is an array
price is looked up by client-supplied sku, with no check that the result is a valid number
qty goes through Math.floor and Math.max(1, ...), which does not reject NaN or Infinity
the possibly NaN or Infinity total is charged

finding.guards_checked: Math.max(1, floor(qty)) blocks zero and negative quantities, so the negative-qty abuse from /checkout is closed here. There is no NaN, finite-number or integer check, no upper bound on qty, and no check that the sku exists. Whether the payment provider rejects NaN is not visible in the repo, so the impact is uncertain.

verdict.guard_found: Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) at cart.js:14 only blocks zero/negative qty; no NaN/finite/integer check, no upper bound, no sku-exists check, no array check, and no auth or validation middleware in this file.
verdict.reason: cart.js:14 multiplies the catalog price by Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) with no finite-number validation, so a non-numeric qty, an unknown sku (undefined price, cart.js:13) or a huge qty yields a NaN or Infinity total that is passed to req.payments.charge at cart.js:16; the impact depends on how the payment provider treats such an amount, which is not visible in the repo, so this is a low-severity input-validation issue.
